pages.c16-p01: Encrypt and decrypt with substitution ciphers and break them using frequency analysis
pages.c16-p02: Explain why key length matters and describe symmetric encryption
pages.c16-p03: Explain how public-key cryptography lets people communicate securely without first sharing a secret key
pages.c16-p04: Describe how HTTPS uses encryption and certificates to protect communication on the web
pages.c16-p05: Explain how hashing protects stored passwords and how end-to-end encryption protects messages
pages.c16-p06: Explain why quantum computers threaten today's public-key encryption and discuss the debate about encryption, privacy and security

q.q: What is cryptography?
o: The science of keeping information secret

q.q: What is plaintext?
What is ciphertext?
What is decryption?
Using a Caesar shift of 3, what does A become?
How many useful shifts does a Caesar cipher have?
q.why: A shift of 26 gives the original.

q.q: What does a substitution cipher do?
o: Replaces each letter with another letter from a secret alphabet
q.why: Any letter can map to any other.

q.q: What is frequency analysis?
o: Counting letter frequencies to break a cipher

q.q: In a long English ciphertext, the most common letter probably stands for...
Who first described frequency analysis?
A one-letter word in a ciphertext is probably...
q.why: Only A and I are one-letter English words.

q.q: What is a brute-force attack?
How many combinations does a 3-dial (0-9) lock have?
How many keys does an 8-bit key have?
How many keys does a 3-bit key have?
Adding one bit to a key...
o: doubles the number of possible keys

q.q: What is the only defence against brute force?
o: Encrypting twice with the same key
Making the number of possible keys enormous

q.q: What is symmetric encryption?
o: Encryption using the same key to lock and unlock

q.q: What does AES stand for?
Which key lengths does AES use?
What is the main problem with symmetric encryption?
Why is symmetric encryption used for most data?
What is key length?
o: The physical size of a key
The number of bits in a key

q.q: What problem does public-key cryptography solve?
o: Sharing secrets with someone you've never met

q.q: Another name for public-key cryptography is...
Which key is shared with everyone?
Which key must be kept secret?
To send Mia a secret message, you encrypt it with...
q.why: Only Mia's private key can then decrypt it.

q.q: Who can decrypt a message encrypted with Mia's public key?
o: Only Mia, with her private key

q.q: In the padlock analogy, the open padlock represents...
What is a one-way function?
o: Easy to calculate but very hard to reverse

q.q: What is 13 × 17?
q.why: Easy to multiply; hard to reverse for big numbers.

q.q: RSA encryption relies on the difficulty of...
o: finding the prime factors of huge numbers

q.q: Which UK organisation's researchers secretly discovered public-key ideas in the 1970s?
q.why: GCHQ's work was kept secret for years.

q.q: What does HTTPS stand for?
What protocol encrypts HTTPS connections?
What was the problem with plain HTTP?
o: Data was sent as readable plain text

q.q: What does a digital certificate prove?
Who issues digital certificates?
What does the padlock in the address bar mean?
o: The connection is encrypted and the certificate matches the address

q.q: Can scam websites use HTTPS?
What is a session key?
o: A temporary key agreed for one connection
q.why: It's used for that session only.

q.q: In HTTPS, which encryption is used to agree the session key?
In HTTPS, which encryption protects the main data?
What should you do if your browser says "Your connection is not private"?
Why is public Wi-Fi risky without HTTPS?
o: Others on the network could read your data

q.q: What does a hash function produce?
o: An encrypted file with a key
A fixed-length fingerprint of the data

q.q: Can a hash be turned back into the original input?
What happens to a hash if you change one letter of the input?
Why do good websites store password hashes?
o: Stolen hashes can't simply be reversed into passwords

q.q: How does a website check your password?
o: It hashes what you type and compares hashes

q.q: What is a salt?
o: Random data added before hashing a password

q.q: Why do salts help?
o: They remove the need for passwords

q.q: A website emails you your actual old password. This suggests...
Does hashing protect weak passwords completely?
o: No: attackers can hash common passwords and compare

q.q: What is end-to-end encryption?
o: The company encrypts at its end only
Encrypting the start and end of a message
Only the sender and receiver can read messages

q.q: With E2EE, what does the app company's server see?
Which app is known for end-to-end encrypted messaging?
Hashes can be used to check that a download hasn't been changed. Why?
o: Any change would produce a completely different hash

q.q: What is a quantum computer?
o: A computer using quantum physics to solve certain problems much faster
A computer from the future that doesn't exist

q.q: Which encryption would a large quantum computer threaten most?
Who discovered the quantum algorithm for factoring?
What is "harvest now, decrypt later"?
o: Storing encrypted data to break with future computers

q.q: What is post-quantum cryptography?
o: Encryption designed to resist quantum computers

q.q: Which organisation published the first post-quantum standards in 2024?
q.why: The US National Institute of Standards and Technology.

q.q: How does a quantum computer affect AES-256?
o: It weakens it a little, but it's still considered strong

q.q: What is an encryption backdoor?
o: A secret way for authorities to read encrypted data

q.q: Which is an argument FOR encryption backdoors?
o: They could help police investigate serious crimes

q.q: Which is an argument AGAINST encryption backdoors?
o: Criminals or hostile states could find and abuse them
q.why: A weakness for one is a weakness for all.

q.q: Why might journalists rely on strong encryption?
Which is a strong password idea?
o: Three random words with a number and symbol

q.q: Mary, Queen of Scots' secret plot was uncovered using...
A 2-digit PIN (00-99) has how many combinations?
A 10-bit key has how many possible keys?
Why is a 128-bit key considered safe from brute force?
o: Trying every key would take longer than the age of the universe

q.q: What is 79 × 83?
q.why: Easy to multiply, hard to factor back.

q.q: Why is the private key never sent over the internet?
o: Anyone intercepting it could decrypt your messages
q.why: Keeping it local keeps it safe.

q.q: Which part of the TLS handshake shows the website's identity?
Why does HTTPS use both kinds of encryption?
o: Public-key solves key sharing; symmetric is fast for data

q.q: Which is NOT a property of a good hash function?
o: You can reverse it with a key

q.q: In a data breach, which stolen data is LEAST useful to criminals?
q.why: Salted hashes are hard to crack.

q.q: Why does end-to-end encryption protect you if the company is hacked?
o: The servers only hold ciphertext they can't read

q.q: Which describes the key-sharing problem?
o: How to agree a secret key safely over a public network
How to cut a metal key

q.q: Who is "Eve" in cryptography examples?
What is the effect of using a 256-bit AES key instead of 128-bit?
o: Far more possible keys and stronger protection

q.q: Why are certificate warnings important?
o: They may mean a fake site or an interception attempt
They mean the site is fast

q.q: Which statement about encryption is true?
o: Strong encryption protects banking, messaging and online shopping
Encryption is illegal in the UK

q.q: What does the UK's National Cyber Security Centre advise organisations about quantum computing?
o: Plan to migrate to post-quantum cryptography over the coming years

q.q: A pupil says "HTTPS means the website can't be a scam." What's wrong?
o: HTTPS sites are all government sites
HTTPS only encrypts the connection; scam sites can use it too

q.q: What is a digital signature used for?
o: Proving a message really came from the sender and wasn't changed
q.why: Signatures use private keys and hashes.

q.q: Which ancient cipher was used by Julius Caesar?
Using a Caesar shift of 3, what does HELLO become?
Decrypt FDW with a Caesar shift of 3.
Why are long messages easier to break with frequency analysis?
o: There are more letters to count, so the pattern is clearer

q.q: A computer tries 1 billion keys per second. Roughly how long to try all 256 keys of an 8-bit key?
q.why: 256 tries is nothing for a computer.

q.q: Which everyday technology uses symmetric encryption?
q.why: Wi-Fi traffic is encrypted with AES.

q.q: In the double-padlock method, why does the box stay locked in transit?
o: At least one padlock is always on it

q.q: Which part of a website address shows it uses HTTPS?
Why is a new session key made for each connection?
o: It's required by the browser's colour
So that one stolen key can't unlock other sessions

q.q: Which is the best reason to use a password manager?
o: It makes all passwords the same
It removes the need for HTTPS
It stores long unique passwords for every site
